note: Build stages and twin designs for the Execution tab. Measured numbers are read by build_page.py from bench/results/twin_designs.json and bench/results/pairs_poc.json; this file holds the plan text only.

stages.makes: questions answered from exact 3D state, the agent loop (typed tool calls, last 4 views + move log, up to 10 moves), a grader for answers and every stated step, no AI judge
stages.now: 13 of 13 tests pass; perfect test agent 100%; lucky agent (right answers, steps 40% off) 0% on steps

stages.makes: 10 twin designs measured on a sparse and a cluttered test warehouse; proof-of-concept set D2 + D4 + D8, each with a D10 keep twin, built pair-first
stages.now: see the Twin designs sub-tab; 20 triples per test scene
stages.next: scale to all 10 designs (Twin designs sub-tab, column 'To scale')

stages.makes: Isaac Sim 6.0.1 (pip, Python 3.12, own venv) loads SimReady Warehouse-01, exports every labelled object as a box into the scene file (repeated names not askable), builds the question triples, renders RGB + depth per view in priority order (start views, then views 2 moves away, then the rest), renders swap twins in their edited scene, and checks rendered depth against the scene file
stages.now: dry run on the Mac with a fake renderer: 20 triples, 984 views written, depth check 254 of 254; a 783-object test scene builds 20 triples in 9 s; 13 tests pass
stages.next: rent an RTX PRO 6000 with driver 595.58.03 or newer, Ubuntu 22.04+, 50 GB free; run bench/stage1_gpu.sh (10-minute smoke, then a 60-minute render cap); during the run, a live walk-through of the warehouse over Isaac Sim's stream (ports 49100 TCP, 47998 UDP)

stages.makes: about 200 questions as triples, through APIs only: OpenAI (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol), Google (Gemini 3.1 Pro, 3.8 Flash), Anthropic (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5), xAI (Grok 4.7), Fireworks (Kimi K3, Inkling, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), Alibaba Cloud (Qwen3.8-Max, after a one-image test); a human-play page on the same renders, scored by the same grader
stages.now: OpenAI and Fireworks ids confirmed from their listings (2026-10-01); Google, Anthropic, xAI and Alibaba keys still to add
stages.next: a 20-triple smoke run on two cheap models first, to read real token counts; then accuracy, step score, triple score, parse failures; a no-image baseline and a label audit on a sample

stages.makes: about 50 triples where the agent moves freely (any step length, any turn) and Isaac Sim renders each view on demand; the same models and the same grader as on the frozen grid
stages.next: done when: the model ranking on the live triples vs the same triples on the frozen grid is reported (rank correlation); it answers row C1 on Rejection Risk. Cost: about 2-4 GPU hours and, with 3-4 models, roughly $50-70 of API calls (estimate)

stages.makes: about 3,000 test questions (about 1,000 triples) across the scenes; the full model list; a human baseline; a label audit on a sample; release files
stages.next: done when: renders pass the depth check, ~1,000 triples are built, models are scored (smoke run, then the full list), and the human baseline and label audit are done

stages.makes: about 50,000 training triples (150,000 questions) with their renders, from seeds disjoint from the private test seed
stages.next: starts when: phase 1 is done; stage 1 has measured views per second and size per view; a scene-variety plan exists (object shuffles, more SimReady scenes); training seeds are fixed. Open: a small fine-tune to show the split helps, or release it as RL-ready data with its training value untested

twins.name: near pair, small move
twins.scale: needs scenes with many object pairs closer than 3 m (real shelving aisles); pick such pairs first

twins.name: camera move
twins.scale: already in the set; record each pair's move and turn; cap the move per scene size

twins.name: camera height
twins.render: a second and third grid height (3x renders)
twins.scale: render the grid at 0.8, 1.5 and 3.0 m; only above-or-below questions flip (visibility never did)

twins.name: object swap
twins.scale: already in the set; move two prims in the USD stage, render the start view again, re-export the scene file

twins.name: object nudge
twins.scale: collision-free placement within 2 m, then the same re-render as D4

twins.name: orbit 180
twins.scale: render the view facing the pair from the far side; moves are large (9 to 11 m)

twins.name: azimuth sweep
twins.scale: render views around the pair in 45-degree steps and keep the smallest that flips

twins.name: frame switch
twins.scale: already in the set; needs a third object visible in the same view

twins.name: occluder in or out
twins.scale: insert a crate prim between camera and object (or remove the blocker), re-render; rare in both test scenes

twins.name: keep-answer twin
twins.scale: already in the set: every pair carries one, making a triple
